svg.title: A Mature Cohort Producing 75 Paid Cases
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-02-mature-cohort-conversion; chart type: funnel; title: A Mature Cohort Producing 75 Paid Cases; subtitle: Nested case populations support $255,000 in Base-Case service fees.; chapter number: 6; epistemic tag: illustrative_model; assumptions note: Illustrative mature cohort, not observed conversion performance. Begin with 1,000 distinct owner-property case IDs; each later population is a subset of the preceding population. Assume 75 completed, fee-paid cases recognized within one modeled year at $3,400 average service fees. This is not a 30-day forecast.; caption: 1,000 × 40% × 40% × 62.5% × 75% = 75 paid cases; 75 × $3,400 = $255,000 recognized service-fee revenue.; stages: label: Screened prospects; value: 1,000 distinct cases enter the research cohort; numeric value: 1000.0; detail: Deduplicate by jurisdiction, property identifier, and reported owner. Exclude repeated outreach records rather than inflating the top of the funnel.; label: Evidence-supported matches; value: 400 cases pass preliminary identity and value screening; numeric value: 400.0; detail: Forty percent of screened cases have a supportable ownership hypothesis and sufficient expected fees to justify additional research; entitlement remains subject to proof.; label: Lawfully engaged owners; value: 160 matched cases obtain valid service agreements; numeric value: 160.0; detail: Forty percent of matched cases proceed after direct-claim disclosure, signer verification, statutory timing checks, and acceptance of a permitted fee structure.; label: Complete claims filed; value: 100 engaged cases reach accepted submission status; numeric value: 100.0; detail: Sixty-two and one-half percent of engagements supply the necessary records. Submission acceptance does not mean the treasury has approved ownership or payment.; label: Recovered and fee-paid; value: 75 filed cases produce recognized and collected fees; numeric value: 75.0; detail: Seventy-five percent of filed cases complete within the modeled recognition year. Remaining cases stay open, withdraw, or fail; do not book their hoped-for fees.

text.title: A Mature Cohort Producing 75 Paid Cases

rect.title: label: Screened prospects; value: 1,000 distinct cases enter the research cohort; numeric value: 1000.0; detail: Deduplicate by jurisdiction, property identifier, and reported owner. Exclude repeated outreach records rather than inflating the top of the funnel.

label: Evidence-supported matches; value: 400 cases pass preliminary identity and value screening; numeric value: 400.0; detail: Forty percent of screened cases have a supportable ownership hypothesis and sufficient expected fees to justify additional research; entitlement remains subject to proof.

label: Lawfully engaged owners; value: 160 matched cases obtain valid service agreements; numeric value: 160.0; detail: Forty percent of matched cases proceed after direct-claim disclosure, signer verification, statutory timing checks, and acceptance of a permitted fee structure.

label: Complete claims filed; value: 100 engaged cases reach accepted submission status; numeric value: 100.0; detail: Sixty-two and one-half percent of engagements supply the necessary records. Submission acceptance does not mean the treasury has approved ownership or payment.

label: Recovered and fee-paid; value: 75 filed cases produce recognized and collected fees; numeric value: 75.0; detail: Seventy-five percent of filed cases complete within the modeled recognition year. Remaining cases stay open, withdraw, or fail; do not book their hoped-for fees.

text.title: Assumptions: Illustrative mature cohort, not observed conversion performance. Begin with 1,000 distinct owner-property case IDs; each later population is a subset of the preceding population. Assume 75 completed, fee-paid cases recognized within one modeled year at $3,400 average service fees. This is not a 30-day forecast.
